question: Polar molecules are the molecules :

options.text: having a permanent electric dipole moment.
acquire a dipole moment only in the presence of electric field due to displacement of charges.
acquire a dipole moment only when magnetic field is absent.

solution:
In a polar molecule (for example H$_2$O or HCl), the centres of positive and negative charge do not coincide even without an external field, so it has a permanent electric dipole moment.

Non-polar molecules have zero dipole moment and acquire one (induced) only in an electric field.
